docRequirement: skills.md:494 — "The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder, so Claude receives actual data, not the command itself." The page binds four properties of that grammar: the placeholder is the inline form `` !`<command>` `` and a skill may carry any number of them (:518 "Each `` !`<command>` `` executes immediately", the pr-summary example at :504-515 carries three inside list items); the output REPLACES the placeholder in place (:519); substitution "runs once over the original file" and output "is not re-scanned for further `` !`<command>` `` placeholders" (:524); the form "is only recognized when `!` appears at the start of a line or immediately after whitespace" and is left as literal text when `!` follows another character, as in `` KEY=!`cmd` `` (:526). A fenced code block opened with ` ```! ` is the documented multi-line form (:528-536).
current: We recognise a different grammar and append instead of substituting. `runtimeSkillContextCommand` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts:19-51) walks the body, toggles a `fenced` flag on any line matching `/^\s*```/` and skips fenced content and blanks (:24-28), takes the FIRST surviving line as `first`, and returns `undefined` unless `first.startsWith('!')` (:32) — so the placeholder must be a whole line at column 0, and leading whitespace disqualifies it. The command is `first.slice(1).trim()` (:33), so backticks are not delimiters and stay inside the command string. A SECOND top-level `!` line throws `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous` (:48), so at most one command per skill is possible. The ` ```! ` fenced form is swallowed by the same fence toggle at :24 and never runs. Consequences of the grammar: the docs' own pr-summary body (three `` !`gh …` `` placeholders inside `- ` list items) and the docs' quickstart `summarize-changes` body both yield `undefined` — zero substitutions; a body whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` yields the command string "`git diff HEAD`", backticks included. Insertion point: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2412 calls the recogniser with `invocation.body`, and :2446 returns `outputs.join('\n\n')`; the call site computes `pinnedSkills` at :2794 BEFORE the context at :2795-2799 and folds the output in as its own `messageParts` block at :2805, i.e. after the whole `<invoked-skill>` element rendered by `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:1075-1077) — never at a placeholder. The only regex in the repo that matches the documented form is the adapter's detector `{ pattern: /!`[^`]*`/, kind: 'bash-execution' }` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:655), which only classifies and defers (:741-749) and performs no substitution. `grep -an '!`'` and `grep -ran '```!'` over packages/apps (excluding dist) find no other implementation. Two further narrowings, already litigated elsewhere and not part of this delta: the path runs only when `runtime?.provider === 'pi'` (base-agent.ts:2407) and only for skills with `pluginRuntime` (:2411), and model-invoked skills render through `buildModelSkillContinuation` (:2659-2679) which never calls the execution path at all. The command string reaches the shell verbatim: SessionManager.ts:4586 builds `{ command: request.command, cwd: pinnedCwd }`, :4588 evaluates it with `shouldAllowToolInMode('Bash', input, …)`, :4598 with `evaluatePermissionDslV1`, :4651 shows it to the user in a `permission_request` event, and :4700 spawns `/bin/sh -lc <approvedCommand>`.
divergence: The execution machinery (permission gate, 5 s timeout, 32 KiB cap, receipts) is right; the placeholder GRAMMAR and the INSERTION POINT are wrong. Five deltas: (1) recogniser shape — a bare `!` that must begin the first non-empty, non-fenced line, versus an inline `` !`<command>` `` legal anywhere `!` follows line start or whitespace (:526); (2) count — exactly one, with a second column-0 `!` line throwing `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous` (runtime-skill-context.ts:48), versus unlimited (:518); (3) delimiters — the backticks are kept as part of the command string by `first.slice(1).trim()` (:33) instead of being stripped as delimiters, so the executed and policy-matched string is `` `git diff HEAD` `` rather than `git diff HEAD`; (4) the ` ```! ` multi-line form (:528-536) is unimplemented and classified as prose by the fence toggle at :24; (5) placement — output is appended as a separate trailing context block (base-agent.ts:2446, :2805) instead of replacing the placeholder in place (:519). Nothing here is a value-versus-key-name mismatch; the timeout, byte cap and executor contract are all fine as they stand.

change.what: Replace the single-command recogniser with a span parser: `export function parseRuntimeSkillContextCommands(body: string): readonly { command: string; start: number; end: number; form: 'inline' | 'fenced' }[]`. One pass over the whole body. Inline form: `!` immediately followed by a backtick where the `!` is at line start or immediately after whitespace, terminated by the next backtick on the same line (skills.md:526) — a `!` preceded by a non-whitespace character (`` KEY=!`cmd` ``) is left literal and yields no match. Fenced form: an opening line matching `/^\s*```!\s*$/`, everything up to the matching closing fence being ONE multi-line command (skills.md:528-536); every other ``` fence stays prose exactly as today. Keep `runtime-skill-context-command-empty` for a placeholder whose inner text is blank. DELETE the `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous` throw at :48 — multiple placeholders are legal. Add `export function applyRuntimeSkillContextOutputs(body: string, matches, outputs: readonly string[]): string` splicing outputs into the spans right-to-left in one pass, so a command's output is never re-scanned (skills.md:524). Keep `RUNTIME_SKILL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT_MS`/`RUNTIME_SKILL_CONTEXT_MAX_BYTES` per command and add an aggregate ceiling (a `RUNTIME_SKILL_CONTEXT_MAX_COMMANDS` and a total-bytes check) so N placeholders cannot push the rendered body past `MAX_SKILL_BODY_BYTES` (runtime-skill-content.ts:8) or `MAX_SKILL_INVOCATION_BYTES` (:14).

Parse the placeholders on the RAW body (post-frontmatter, pre-expansion) and replace each span with an opaque sentinel BEFORE the variable and `$ARGUMENTS` passes at :645-698, carrying the parsed command list on the invocation. Reason: `skills.md:524` binds substitution to the original file, and today's recogniser runs on the already-expanded `invocation.body`; once every placeholder is executable, a user-supplied `$ARGUMENTS` value containing `` !`…` `` would otherwise become an executable placeholder. Leave `SkillInvocationRecord.body` (:39) holding the sentinel/original text so `invocationDigest`, `assertSkillInvocationBudget` (:272) and the persisted continuation snapshot keep describing the source, not volatile command output.

Add an optional rendered-body parameter — `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation(invocation, renderedBody = invocation.body)` at :1075 — and interpolate `renderedBody` in place of `invocation.body` at :1077, so the substituted text is what the model sees while the record stays unchanged.

Turn `materializeRuntimeSkillContext` (:2401) into a body renderer: for each invocation parse every placeholder, run each command through the existing executor call at :2424 with the same abort/timeout/byte wiring, then `applyRuntimeSkillContextOutputs` and return a `Map<skillKey, renderedBody>`; delete `outputs.join('\n\n')` at :2446. `formatPinnedSkillInstructions` (:2395) takes that map and forwards each rendered body to `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation`. At the call site move :2794 to AFTER the await at :2795-2799 and drop `runtimeSkillContext` from `messageParts` at :2805. Decide explicitly what a reinjection turn renders: :2407 returns '' today, so a reinjected body must fall back to the sentinel-stripped original rather than to stale output.

No contract change — it stays one call per placeholder (:4521-4726) — but a doc-conformant skill now makes N sequential calls, so N permission decisions (:4586-4618), N `permission_request` events (:4651) and N `skill-context` receipts (:4624-4632) per invocation. Confirm that is the intended UX or batch the decision. The command string authorized at :4586 and spawned at :4700 loses its backticks, which is precisely what lets an `allowed-tools: Bash(gh *)`-style rule match instead of falling through to a prompt.

change.symbol: 'reads one top-level first-line skill context command…' / 'rejects empty or repeated…'
change.what: The assertions at :48-50 and :54-55 encode the old grammar and must be rewritten. Add as positive fixtures the docs' own pr-summary body (skills.md:504-515, three inline placeholders in list items → three substitutions in place), a ` ```! ` multi-line block, `` KEY=!`cmd` `` staying literal (:526), and a placeholder inside an ordinary ```sh fence staying prose. Update the fixture body at :82 and the ordering assertions at :90-98, which currently assert the appended-block layout.
One line: import the new parser's inline regex here instead of the private `/!`[^`]*`/` at :655, so what the adapter detects and defers and what the runtime executes cannot drift apart.

blastRadius: `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation` has three production callers — base-agent.ts:2398 (pinned user-turn skills), base-agent.ts:2677 (`buildModelSkillContinuation`, which never runs the execution path, so a model-invoked skill would keep rendering unsubstituted placeholders unless it is wired too) and packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11021 (the Pi child-session prompt, where a deliberate decision is needed on whether a child sees substituted output) — plus four assertions in packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/runtime-skill-content.test.ts:204, :451, :484, :512. `SkillInvocationRecord.body` CROSSES A PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY: it is digested into `invocationDigest`, snapshotted into packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/continuation-envelope.ts:19, re-validated by `validateSkillInvocationSnapshot` (runtime-skill-content.ts:278) and budgeted by `assertSkillInvocationBudget` against `MAX_SKILL_INVOCATION_BYTES` = 1 MiB (:13-14, :272) — keeping the record original and substituting only at render time avoids a schema change and keeps command output out of session state; substituting into the record does not, and is a risk trigger. The permission path is the other boundary: SessionManager.ts:4586 canonical input, :4588 `shouldAllowToolInMode('Bash', …)`, :4598 `evaluatePermissionDslV1` with `semanticId: 'skill-context'`, :4651 the user-visible `permission_request` event, :4625 the Pi execution receipt — the authorized string changes shape (backticks dropped) and its count per turn changes from at most one to N. Imported-plugin path: any Claude plugin skill written to the documented syntax starts executing where it previously did nothing, so the trust and `disableSkillShellExecution` story (findings f059/f213, both refuted, admin denial today via the managed permission DSL) should be re-read before landing. packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/extension-first/claude-parity-evidence.test.ts:47 references `runtime-skill-context.test.ts` by path as parity evidence. packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:241-250 documents the `shell` field against "our inline expansion has one shell" — still true, but its wording assumes this grammar.
userImpact: A user installs a Claude plugin whose skill uses the documented syntax — the page's own pr-summary is the canonical case — invokes it on the Pi backend, and nothing runs: `runtimeSkillContextCommand` returns `undefined`, so the model receives the literal text `- PR diff: !`gh pr diff`` and answers with no PR data, or decides to call Bash itself, which the page explicitly says should not happen ("This is preprocessing, not something Claude executes"). The same for any ` ```! ` block. If the plugin author instead puts a single placeholder at column 0 on the first body line, the user gets a Bash approval prompt showing the backtick-wrapped string `` `git diff HEAD` `` — which the skill's own `allowed-tools: Bash(git diff:*)` rule cannot match, so it prompts where it should have been silent — and, if approved, `/bin/sh -lc` (SessionManager.ts:4700) performs command substitution rather than running the command, exits non-zero and fails the turn with `runtime-skill-context-command-failed`. A skill with two column-0 `!` lines fails the whole turn with `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous`, uncaught at base-agent.ts:2412. On any non-Pi backend, for any non-plugin skill, and for model-invoked skills, none of this executes at all, so there the impact is only the un-expanded placeholder text.

Not re-litigated here and deliberately excluded from the delta: the pi-only / pluginRuntime-only gates (finding f059) and the absent first-party `disableSkillShellExecution` reader (f213) — both were refuted as separate rows.
